newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's UES plans ADR issue, convertible bond.
newsitem.headline: Russia's UES plans ADR issue, convertible bond.

text.p: Russia's national power company Unified Energy System (UES) plans to isssue American Depositary Receipts on its shares this summer to increase company liquidity before issuing convertible bonds this autumn, UES treasurer Alexander Lopatin said on Thursday.

"Since in autumn this year we plan to issue convertible bonds to increase liquidity and improve the image of the company, we need to issue ADRs, and that will be, no doubt, in the summer," Lopatin told Reuters
Boris Brevnov, UES's chief executive, said the convertible bond could be issued by autumn, which is slightly sooner than Lopatin said.
"We plan to issue convertible bonds by autumn, but before that we will enter the capital market," Brevnov told a news conference.
Lopatin, who was speaking on the sidelines of the same conference, said UES would do all it could to avoid handing over assets, including power stations, to Russia's gas monopoly Gazprom GAZP.RTS.
First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko said last week the government was considering transferring assets from UES to Gazprom as a way of cancelling mutual debts.
